text:
Hello,

Attached is the letter I received from my landlord, Rosenau Services Ltd, on 10 March 2026.

In it Mr Ian Marti tells me that the rent for my flat at Rosenweg 121 in Wil will rise from CHF 2030 to CHF 2195 a month from 1 July 2026. That is CHF 165 a month, or almost CHF 2000 a year, which is a lot for a pensioner.

The increase has nothing to do with any index. My lease does not tie the rent to the consumer price index or anything similar, and the letter doesn't mention an index either.

What the letter does say is that Rosenau's own costs have gone up: higher heating oil and electricity prices for the common areas, a large rise in the building insurance premium, and higher costs for caretaking and maintenance. Mr Marti writes that these have to be passed on fairly to the tenants. I don't doubt that energy is more expensive, but I pay my heating and service costs separately on account every month already, so I don't understand why they should also go into my basic rent. My neighbour Peter Shaw got the same letter and thinks it's a way of charging us twice.

I've also attached my lease so you can check the terms. Can you tell me whether this increase is justified and whether I should contest it?

With thanks,
Peter Vogel

Rosenau Services Ltd
Wil, 6 March 2026

Mr Peter Vogel
Rosenweg 121
9500 Wil

Your flat at Rosenweg 121

Dear Mr Vogel,

We are writing to let you know about a change to the rent for your flat. Up to now you have paid CHF 2030 per month. From 1 July 2026 the rent will be CHF 2195 per month.

The reason is that the costs of running the property have risen considerably over the past two years. In particular, the energy costs for the common areas, the premiums for the building insurance and the costs of caretaking and maintenance are now markedly higher. We are obliged to pass these higher costs on fairly to our tenants.

We thank you for your understanding and remain at your disposal for any questions.

Yours sincerely,

Rosenau Services Ltd
Ian Marti
